sections.title: Overview
sections.html:
• Reference date: 2026-10-28 (KST) · run id 2026-10-28-event · mode event (incremental) · previous run 2026-10-27-event-r2 (6th run) · previous monthly run 2026-10 (Source: run information injected by the workflow · _probe/context.json)
  • Reason: The news monitor detected two clusters of reports on 2026-10-28, "Amazon's $11.5 billion Globalstar deal gets FCC approval" (advanced television · businessline · fierce network) and "Amazon's Leo Gets FCC Clearance To Buy Globalstar" (citinewsroom · finimize, etc.), and launched this run by linking them to T4 (Amazon Leo US consumer commercial launch regions and pricing) — the reports are not a basis for judgment but an item to verify (Source: data/spacex_watch.json due news:amazon-globalstar-fcc:2026-10-28 · news:amazon-leo-globalstar-fcc:2026-10-28, 2026-10-28 11:39 KST)
  • Reference share price: $148.58 — close on 2026-10-27 (Tue), volume 95.86 million shares. +1.1% versus the previous run's reference price of $146.90 (10/26) (formula: 148.58 ÷ 146.90 − 1) (stockanalysis daily history, accessed 2026-10-28: latest row 10/27)
  • Scope: Only what this event touches — trigger T4 (verdict: not applicable), the D2D (satellite-to-phone) axis of the competition timeline, the background facts for milestone A-2028-1 (separate Starlink Mobile disclosure), and the new trigger T8. Also recorded is SpaceX's own FCC D2D authorization (10/6, DA 26-1078), which surfaced in the same reporting. Axes B–D, probabilities and fair value are not recalculated (Source: prompts/monthly_run.md · state.triggers_next_12m).
Conclusion first: The reports are accurate — on 2026-10-27 the FCC Space Bureau, Wireless Telecommunications Bureau and International Bureau approved the application to transfer Globalstar's licenses and authorizations to Amazon via DA 26-1160 (GN Docket 26-134) (adopted and released on 10/27; conditions: continued compliance with the 1999/2004 LoAs, and Yippy's petition to deny was dismissed). However, this is not the event T4 asks about. T4 is "Amazon Leo US consumer commercial launch regions and pricing," whereas this approval is permission to acquire roughly 25MHz of D2D (satellite-to-phone) spectrum plus Globalstar's satellites and the Apple contract — consumer broadband pricing and regions are still unannounced (checked leo.amazon.com on 10/28, no pricing). Therefore no change to the T4 verdict · rule R5 not triggered · no change to the verdicts of the 29 milestones · probabilities 25/50/25 · value $32 unchanged. What changed: ① the competition timeline now has a D2D axis — Amazon enters via Globalstar (about 24 satellites, Apple 20% stake, closing expected 2027) and from 2028 will deploy its own 5,105 D2D satellites; ② in the same month SpaceX also received an FCC D2D authorization (15,000 satellites, VLEO, DA 26-1078, 10/6), which neither the measurement layer nor the October issue captured — the condition that 2GHz MSS operation is tied to after the EchoStar phase 2 closing (expected 2027-11-30) becomes background for A-2028-1; ③ new trigger T8 (D2D competition) was added, and T4's expected method was revised to reflect Vulcan LV-01 slipping to November (Source: sections 1–6 below).

It is absent from the measurement layer (filings, IR, launch monitoring — news monitoring only from 10/27) and from the 10/23 monthly round. We open the primary source after the event (the original FCC order text) and record it.

What this means for A-2028-1 ("30 million subscribers AND $3 billion in separately disclosed Starlink Mobile (D2C) revenue"): The regulatory door has opened, but 2GHz MSS (EchoStar spectrum) operation is tied to a date after around 2027-11-30. For $3 billion of D2C revenue to appear in the 2028 judgment year, the question is which path reaches the revenue line: ① before the end of 2027, through SCS (carrier spectrum, T-Mobile type) and overseas D2C, or ② through 2GHz MSS during 2028. This round does not change the status (remains in progress, same reason for non-measurability) — because there is no revenue disclosure. However, the two additional primary-source records before 12/1 (DA 26-1078 · the EchoStar second-closing schedule) are not written into progress but attached to open_questions and T8 (source: state.milestones[A-2028-1] · table above).

Monitoring gap record: The 10/6 SpaceX D2D authorization is not subject to a company 8-K and had no IR press release, so it is the kind of event that filing and IR monitoring cannot catch. The news monitor has run since 10/27. sections.title: 4 Competition Timeline Update — New D2D Axis
sections.html:
The October issue's table 1-7 described Amazon Leo only as a "real threat to consumer broadband in 2027–2028." D2D is a revenue item in the Axis A milestone (A-2028-1), and it is the same market as the 800MHz terrestrial network strategy that the October issue described as "the side posing the threat." Starting with this issue, D2D is counted separately.

How to read this: What Amazon gains right now from this approval is spectrum rights and the Apple contract, not subscribers or revenue. The SpaceX-side door (DA 26-1078) opened 3 weeks earlier and is larger in scale (15,000 vs. 5,105 applied for), but both companies remain tied to regulatory and deal conditions until late 2027–2028. This timeline is exactly why the Axis A 2028 milestone requires separate disclosure of D2D revenue (Source: table above).
